content.text: Many NDA applicants are still in Class 12 and are filling a UPSC form for the first time. The uploads are the same as for the Civil Services exam, but a few things catch first-timers out.
Three things first-timers get wrong
One signature instead of three.
UPSC wants your signature three times, one below the other, in one image. The image is roughly square, 350–500 px on each side, 20–100 KB, in black ink.
A school ID-card photo.

The uploaded photo must be recent, in colour, on a white background, with your face filling about 75% of the frame and both ears visible. A cropped group photo or an old ID-card picture will not match your live photo.
A different look on exam day.
The form captures a live photo and compares it with the uploaded one. Avoid a new haircut or beard between the photo and the application.
Step by step
Create your UPSC One-Time Registration if you have not already. The photo and photo ID go in there.
Take the photo against a white wall. JPG, 20–200 KB; SahiSize keeps a 3.5×4.5 cm shape.
On white paper, draw a 6×6 cm square and sign three times inside it. Photograph it and choose NDA here; the crop locks to a square.
Prepare the photo ID you will name in the form. Guides describe it as a PDF of 20–200 KB; check the size and format on the form.
Keep all files. The same OTR serves CDS and other UPSC exams later.
Under 18 and filling the form
The three signatures must be yours, even if a parent helps with the rest of the form. Sign the way you will sign the attendance sheet at the exam.
If you do not have a government photo ID of your own yet, sort that out before the form opens; the ID number you enter must belong to the card you upload and carry.
Timing
NDA is held twice a year. Notifications usually appear around December and May.
If the portal still rejects it

Most rejections are size or shape. A three-signature image under 350 px a side fails, so crop from the original photo, not a screenshot. A photo under 20 KB fails, so do not use a WhatsApp-forwarded copy.
